title: Local IST formatting is hard-coded and ignores each event’s configured timezone

original_titles.title: Timestamps hardcoded to IST; no UTC tooltip; event timezone column ignored
Time zone hardcoded to Asia/Kolkata with literal 'IST' instead of the event's zone
UI timezone formatter hard-codes Asia/Kolkata instead of taking the event timezone
Scheduling/timezone handling thinner than specified (no T-minus calendar, IST hardcoded)
Clock offset estimated from a single sample instead of lowest-RTT multi-sample
Clock offset estimated from a single sample

problem: frontend/src/lib/format.ts hard-codes Asia/Kolkata and appends literal IST. Event records include timezone, but the formatter does not receive it. Clock offset is estimated from a single sample.
impact: Events in other zones display incorrect wall-clock dates/times and daylight-saving/offset behavior is not represented. Single-sample clock sync can produce avoidable countdown drift under network latency.

verification.basis: Current source inspection at the main-branch commit listed in metadata. Original audit line numbers are treated as historical and were not reused as current line references.

implementation_steps.action: Change date/time formatting helpers to accept an IANA timezone from the selected event. Use UTC for machine serialization and event timezone only for display.
Expose timezone as part of event/session context and pass it into every schedule, deadline, announcement and admin timestamp formatter.
Use multiple server-time samples and select the lowest-RTT sample to estimate clock offset; periodically resync on visibility/online transitions.
Add tests for Asia/Kolkata plus a DST-observing zone, midnight boundaries, events with different zones and countdown behavior under latency.

acceptance_criteria: Two events in different zones display their respective local time.
Countdown uses server-anchored time and remains stable after tab wake/network reconnect.
regression_tests: Add a focused failing test before implementation where practical.
Add a negative authorization / boundary test, not only a happy-path test.
Run the affected backend/frontend suite and the full CI workflow before merge.
